_: Generated once by migrate-stock.mjs from the HAVE / USEFIRST / SHOP / ING_NAME tables that used to live in kitchen.html. From here this file is the SEED and stock/events.jsonl is what actually moves. Do not hand-edit a state: append an event instead, or the next fold will overwrite you.

states.have: in the kitchen and usable now
states.frozen: owned, in the freezer, not edible tonight without a thaw

capers.note: Great Value 90 mL jar, Walmart house brand, bought 2026-08-09. The buy block that used to sit here said Walmart does not carry capers in a normal jar size and kept piccata blocked for five days. It was simply false. Keep the jar in the fridge once opened, where it lasts months under its own brine.

buy.walk: Baking aisle, near the flour and sugar
buy.s: WALMART MARKED THIS UNAVAILABLE on the Aug 4 delivery, so it is the one thing from that order you do not have. Every Peruvian source for the arroz tapado uses it and your spice rack has nothing that stands in for it. The dish still works without it, just flatter, and the app tells you how to compensate. $2.27, and any grocery or corner store has it, so do not wait for another Walmart order

yellowonion.note: Yellow, confirmed by Silvio 2026-08-12. This row was briefly renamed to "sweet onions" on the strength of the 2026-08-04 receipt note recording a Walmart substitution; he corrected it the same day. A substitution logged at order time describes that order, not a standing fact about the pantry. White onions are a separate item.

yogurt.label: Greek yogurt, 750 g
yogurt.note: Completely untouched since Aug 1. Not urgent, but it is the single biggest unused thing in the fridge and four jars of overnight oats would take 680 g of it.

peppers.label: Red bell peppers, 2
peppers.note: Off the clearance rack, so they were already partway through their life when they arrived. Treat them as days, not the usual fortnight.

cucumbers.label: English cucumbers, 2
cucumbers.note: Pickling turns these into something that lasts a month instead of a fortnight.

sweetpotato.label: Sweet potato, 1 kg
sweetpotato.note: Keep it out of the fridge, somewhere cool and dark. Cold turns its starch to sugar and gives it a hard core that never softens.

arugula.label: Arugula, about 120 g
arugula.note: The most perishable thing in the kitchen. Bagged greens turn to slime rather than going obviously off, so there is no warning.

beef.label: Browned beef, 3 bags (700 g)
beef.note: Cooked and bagged the evening of Aug 4: 250 g, 250 g and 200 g. Browned beef gets 3 to 4 days in the fridge against 1 to 2 raw. Anything you will not cook by Friday goes in the freezer, where it keeps 3 months.

buy.walk: Rice and pasta aisle. Often shelved with international foods
buy.s: What Korean pot rice is actually made with. Bulgogi and Mushroom Pot Rice works properly with this and only approximately without it. Price seen on walmart.ca 2026-08-04, range was $5.77 to $18.97, so buy the cheap end. Any bag labelled sushi rice, calrose or short-grain is the right thing.

lemon_fresh.note: Distinct from the bottle on purpose. In a sauce where lemon is one of three flavours, they are not the same ingredient. Bought 2026-08-09 as a 908 g bag.

parsley.note: Bought 2026-08-04 for Chicken Piccata and reported going mushy on 2026-08-08. Events for it were already in the database with no catalogue row here, which meant the validator could not resolve any recipe that reached for it. Added 2026-08-09.

turkeydeli.note: Deli slices, already cooked. High in sodium per the label, so anything built on it needs less added salt.

chickendeli.note: Fully cooked deli slices. Deliberately a separate id from `chickenbreast`, which is raw and frozen. A recipe that reaches for one must never resolve to the other.

pineapple.note: Frozen chunks. Raw pineapple carries bromelain, an enzyme that breaks protein down, so it curdles dairy if left to sit and it will not set in gelatin. Fine in a shake drunk straight away.

montereyjack.note: Semi-soft, melts smoothly, jalapeno already in it. Where mozzarella stretches, this one flows, so it suits a quesadilla or eggs rather than a pizza.

spaghetti_cooked.note: Distinct from the dry Barilla in the pantry on purpose: a recipe that wants cold cooked pasta must never resolve to a box of dry pasta, and one that wants dry must never resolve to this. Same reasoning as chickendeli versus chickenbreast. Plain, no sauce, confirmed by Silvio 2026-08-12. Cooked pasta gets 3 to 5 days.

chickenwings.note: Drumette and winglet, bone-in. Freeze-by on the label is Aug 21.

chickenthighs.note: Bone-in skin-on. At $7.63/kg this is the cheapest protein per dollar in the kitchen. Freeze-by Aug 21. Deliberately separate from chickenbreast and from the deli slices: a recipe wanting thighs must never resolve to breast, which cooks differently and dries out.

basil.note: 28 g packet. The most perishable thing in the kitchen, 2 to 3 days. Hates cold: stand the stems in water on the counter or keep it in the fridge DOOR, never the coldest shelf. Not interchangeable with dried basil or with Italian seasoning in anything where it goes in raw at the end.

blackvinegar.note: Catalogued 2026-08-18, not owned. Chinkiang, also spelled Zhenjiang, is a dark malty rice vinegar and it is NOT the distilled white vinegar in the cupboard: it is the sour note in General Tso and in most northern Chinese sauces. Gold Plum 554 ml was $2.99 at Superstore on 2026-08-18. Walmart lists Hengshun at $3.97 on an alphanumeric SKU, which is the marketplace pattern, so the shelf is unproven there.

driedchilli.note: Catalogued 2026-08-18, not owned. Distinct from the fresh chilli gap, from chili powder and from crushed red pepper: these are whole dried pods that go into hot oil for aroma. Omnivore Cookbook General Tso wants 7 to 8 and her footnote says they add aroma rather than heat. Tastie Dried Red Chili 120 g was $2.29 at Superstore on 2026-08-18, and it is not sold as Chinese or Korean, which is his call to make.

tomatoes_round.note: Round slicing tomatoes on the vine, 5 of them, receipt photo 20260814_121315 and the count stated by Silvio. Distinct from the grape tomatoes and from anything tinned. Catalogued 2026-08-18: it had existed only as stock_event 74, so validate.mjs refused a recipe pointing at it and the app printed the raw id where a name belongs.

beanmedley.note: UNCERTAIN COUNT, per stock_event 71: two receipt photos seven seconds apart may be one can twice or two cans, recorded as 1. Ask before a recipe leans on two. Catalogued 2026-08-18 for the same reason as tomatoes_round, and because burrito and chilli recipes are rejected for kidney beans while this sits in the pantry unmatched.

tomatoes_grape.note: 1.5 lb / 680 g, clearance. The first FRESH tomato in this kitchen. Distinct from tinned chopped tomatoes, from tomato sauce and from tomato paste, all of which behave differently in a sauce. Keep on the counter: the fridge kills the flavour and makes the texture mealy.

whiteonion.note: Two, bought 2026-08-12. NOT the same as the sweet onions under `yellowonion`, and the difference matters: white is sharper and cleaner, sweet holds more sugar and water and collapses faster. Recipes asking specifically for white onion can now be satisfied exactly instead of substituted.

sriracha.note: Listed under fridge condiments in KITCHEN.md. Had an alias set but NO catalogue row, so it could never be in stock and 190 recipe lines reported a shortage of something he owns.

pesto.note: KITCHEN.md: "Pesto | a little". Was aliased to peanutbutter, so the app named the wrong jar.

ketchup.note: KITCHEN.md fridge condiments. Was aliased to mayo.

beef-raw.note: Distinct from `beef`, which is BROWNED beef already cooked and bagged. Two different foods that a recipe treats completely differently, and printing them one above the other as "ground beef" twice is what read as a broken app on 2026-08-13. Events have existed for this id since 2026-08-11; the catalogue row was missing until 2026-08-14, which made every recipe pointing at it fail validation.

brownsugar.note: NOT the white sugar. Added to the catalogue 2026-08-14 because it is the single thing standing between this kitchen and a published Mongolian ground beef recipe it otherwise satisfies exactly (Salt & Lavender, 4.92 from 25 ratings). Her sauce is a third of a cup of it. White sugar, honey and maple syrup are all in the cupboard and any of them is a substitution, which only Silvio may decide.
